I’m checking the native preference API and the existing dependency surface before recommending a design.

content.text:
The discussion raises a valid enhancement, but it is more than adding `-array` and `-dict` flags.

Current behavior is intentional:

- `DefaultsValue` only models scalar TOML values; arrays and tables return `None` and are skipped. See [defaults.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/15f9/mise/src/system/defaults.rs:31).
- Config loading deliberately retains raw TOML so newer structured values remain forward-compatible, then warns and skips unsupported shapes in [system/mod.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/15f9/mise/src/system/mod.rs:712).
- The limitation is explicitly documented and tested in [macos-defaults.md](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/15f9/mise/docs/bootstrap/macos-defaults.md:105) and [test_system_defaults](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/15f9/mise/e2e/cli/test_system_defaults:42).

The important complication is macOS’s `defaults` CLI. I tested both available representations:

- `-array`/`-dict` cannot nest composite types; `defaults` exits with `Cannot nest composite types (arrays and dictionaries)`.
- Passing an OpenStep-style nested plist preserves the array/dictionary structure, but converts nested booleans, integers, and floats into strings.

Consequently, simply translating TOML into command-line arguments would corrupt typed Dock entries.

The sound implementation is:

1. Extend `DefaultsValue` recursively with arrays and dictionaries.
2. Convert recursively between TOML and property-list values.
3. On macOS, read and write through Core Foundation’s `CFPreferencesCopyAppValue` / `CFPreferencesSetAppValue`, followed by synchronization. These APIs accept an arbitrary typed property-list object and update one key without exporting and re-importing the entire domain. [Apple documents these APIs specifically for typed preference values](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/corefoundation/preferences-utilities).
4. Compare dictionaries structurally and arrays in order for `status`.
5. Update JSON/status formatting and decide how composite values appear in `--dry-run`, because there is no equivalent safe, copy-pasteable `defaults write` command.
6. Add macOS tests covering arrays of nested dictionaries with strings, booleans, integers, and floats.

I would favor generic typed `[bootstrap.macos.defaults]` support over a dedicated Dock section. It solves the reported use case and every similar preference without encoding Dock-specific behavior.

Two semantic details should be documented:

- Raw keys are exact: the Dock key must be `"persistent-apps"`, not `persistent_apps`.
- The configured array would replace the entire Dock list. Config hierarchy merging still happens at `(domain, key)` level; individual array entries would not merge.

Overall assessment: worthwhile and technically feasible, with moderate implementation complexity. The discussion’s proposed syntax already fits the parser; the main work is replacing the scalar-oriented I/O and comparison layer. No repository changes were made. [Discussion #12942](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/12942).
